papers.title: A discrete realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model and the Schmid transition
papers.abstract: The phase diagram of the boundary sine-Gordon model (bsG), or equivalently of the resistively shunted Josephson junction, has been the subject of recent debate. We introduce a discrete model that reproduces exactly the properties of the bsG model and can be simulated extremely efficiently using cluster Monte Carlo algorithms. This enables us to explore a broad range of parameters and compute the complete universal crossover between the weak- and strong-tunneling regimes. We establish the self-duality of the model and unambiguously identify the vertical line of critical fixed points characteristic of the Schmid transition, recovering the conformal field theory predictions along this line with high accuracy. We further clarify the essential distinctions between the Schmid and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Our results definitively establish the existence and nature of the Schmid transition and demonstrate the validity of the Schmid-Bulgadaev scenario.

papers.title: Quantum Hall Fabry-Pérot Interferometry in Monolayer WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Electronic Fabry-Pérot interferometers provide a powerful probe of coherent quantum Hall edge transport, yet the presence of multiple spin and valley degrees of freedom in existing van der Waals material platforms can complicate their interpretation. Monolayer WSe$_2$ offers a distinct opportunity because strong spin-orbit coupling and spin-valley locking lift these degeneracies, producing intrinsically single-component Landau levels. Here we realize the first gate-defined quantum Hall Fabry-Pérot interferometer in monolayer WSe$_2$. By continuously tuning the cavity size in a single device, we observe robust Aharonov-Bohm (AB) interference of quantum Hall edge channels across the interferometer; the observed predominance in the AB regime is consistent with a weak bulk-edge coupling ($Δ\approx 0.034$) estimated by electrostatics. Moreover, temperature and bias dependence measurements consistently yield an edge velocity $v \approx (4.9 \pm 0.2) \times 10^4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Our results establish monolayer WSe$_2$ as a clean, flavor-resolved platform for quantum Hall interferometry and provide a foundation for future studies of single-component fractional quantum Hall states and interferometric probes of anyonic statistics in transition-metal dichalcogenides.

papers.title: Hidden universality of rare fluctuations and a central-limit structure at criticality
papers.abstract: The central limit theorem is among the most fundamental principles in the natural sciences, governing the fluctuations of sums of weakly correlated random variables through Gaussian statistics. At critical points, however, long-range correlations invalidate this paradigm, raising a fundamental question: does any general limit theorem survive at criticality? Although scale invariance has long been recognised as the defining feature of typical critical fluctuations, the behaviour of rare fluctuations has remained largely unexplored, as their extraordinarily small probabilities place them beyond the reach of conventional numerical methods. Recent theoretical advances suggest that universal asymptotic laws {may govern large deviations in systems at criticality}, yet direct numerical evidence has been lacking. Here we provide the first such evidence in the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Using large-scale Tethered Monte Carlo simulations, we probe order-parameter fluctuations with probabilities as small as $10^{-200}$ and show that, once normalised by their characteristic width, the far tails collapse onto a single asymptotic law shared by distinct microscopic models in the same universality class. This collapse is governed by a universal amplitude, whose numerical extraction is compatible with the conjectured exact result we derive from conformal field theory, and points towards a generalised central limit theorem for critical fluctuations.

papers.title: Symmetry-Enabled Rolling of Composite Bosons: A Route to Superconductivity from Strong Repulsion with $T_c$ Proportional to the Electron Bandwidth
papers.abstract: Motivated by superconductors discovered in systems with a strong Coulomb repulsion, we ask whether such a repulsion can give rise to superconductivity with a transition temperature $T_c$ bounded only by the electron bandwidth. Coulomb repulsion can produce pairing as it binds electrons to holes. If each hole binds three electrons into a three-electron-one-hole (3e1h) composite, the condensation of these bosonic composites can give rise to superconductivity. However, the resulting $T_c$ falls far below the electron bandwidth in the controlled regime where the binding is much stronger than the carriers' kinetic energy. This is because, on a lattice, a tightly bound composite usually has to move through a higher-order process where the intermediate state costs an energy of order the binding energy, so that the strong binding makes the composite heavy, limiting the superfluid stiffness and hence $T_c$. Here, we show that symmetry offers a way around this tradeoff. In lattices satisfying certain symmetry requirements, a composite can move by single-particle hops without any costly intermediate state, a motion we call rolling. Such rolling keeps the mass of the composite finite even for an infinitely strong binding, so that a $T_c$ proportional to the electron bandwidth can be achieved in the controlled regime. We derive a criterion for rolling and apply it to construct all fourteen minimal lattice models that support such rolling. We show that rollable 3e1h composites can indeed be stabilized in the ground state. We then propose to realize such superconductivity in a dual-gate bilayer, and use exact numerics to show that $T_c$ can reach a few percent of the electron hopping. These results establish rollability as a guiding principle in the search for and design of superconductors in strongly repelling electron systems, with the minimal models constructed here as prototypes.

papers.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.

papers.title: Carbon-made Lobachevsky surfaces
papers.abstract: Carbon-made surfaces of constant negative Gaussian curvature realize portions of the Lobachevsky plane in the laboratory, with motivations ranging from analogue gravity, where the elliptic, Beltrami and hyperbolic pseudospheres correspond to the three static phases of the Bañados--Teitelboim--Zanelli black hole, to water desalination. We review and extend their construction around a single principle, the balanced Gauss--Bonnet theorem: the curvature fixed by the topology is shared among disclination defects, elastically deformed hexagons and boundaries. Curvature without defects cannot change the topology: a sphere made of hexagons only is a punctured sphere, as an explicit polyhedral construction shows. The arrangements of the defects on the three pseudospheres stem from the elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic one-parameter subgroups of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: we construct them for the elliptic family, recover the known one of the Beltrami pseudosphere, and propose one for the hyperbolic pseudosphere. We compare these ideal arrangements with carbon structures obtained by design and by simulated nano-extrusion, and suggest that the infinitely many Fuchsian groups may correspond to the infinitely many Lobachevsky surfaces.

papers.title: Little-Parks Oscillations and Parity Effects in Mesoscopic Superconducting Rings
papers.abstract: We analytically investigate the Little-Parks (LP) effect, the periodic oscillation of the superconducting transition temperature $T_c$ driven by an applied magnetic flux $Φ$, from the weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) limit to the intermediate-coupling regime in a mesoscopic, quasi-one-dimensional ring. Utilizing a Ginzburg-Landau (GL) expansion with twisted boundary conditions, we correctly incorporate both the discrete finite-size topological parity interference and the continuous center-of-mass (CM) kinetic energy shift induced by the supercurrent. We derive a closed-form expression for $T_c(Φ)$ valid within the GL framework across variable interaction strengths. We demonstrate that the LP response comprises two distinct physical contributions: a discrete topological parity effect governed by the correlation length ratio $ξ/R$, and a continuous kinetic energy term scaling as $1/R^2$. As the coupling increases and the spatial correlation length of the pairs contracts ($ξ\ll R$), the constituent pairs become geometrically blind to the global boundary constraint, leading to an exponential suppression of the discrete parity modulation. However, the requirement that the condensate acquires a flux-dependent macroscopic CM momentum persists. This ensures that the critical temperature $T_c$ maintains an algebraic LP modulation driven predominantly by the macroscopic kinetic energy of the supercurrent. We bound our theoretical approach by discussing the breakdown of mean-field GL validity before phase fluctuations dominate near the strong-coupling limit.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论解析研究；基于Ginzburg-Landau展开推导；研究对象：介观准一维超导环，弱耦合BCS极限至中间耦合区

papers.title: Rational layers in the low temperature expansion of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: A low-temperature expansion orders Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can occur at the same order. We instead organize the zero-field simple-cubic model by the excess above the minimum wall area compatible with two prescribed spans. We prove that every fixed excess layer, including all logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, has a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1 - x, 1 - y and 1 - x - y. The proof compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations and assigns each unbounded interval to one monotone chain. A finite controller then enforces induced contacts and arbitrary cover-color reuse. We explicitly assemble the complete layers of excess zero through three over all widths, attributing their known geometric constituents to earlier polyomino enumeration. Exact lattice checks corroborate the formulas. A certified low-temperature comparison shows a modest hybrid accuracy gain at one sampling point and higher evaluation cost. The result establishes an exact layer structure; summation over unbounded excess remains a separate problem.

papers.title: Quantitative Gaussian limits of periodic O(N) models at and below the critical temperature
papers.abstract: We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour $O(N)$ model on periodic boxes of side $M$ in $d\ge3$, at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large $M,N$, the unnormalized $1$-Wasserstein error for the first $p\le N$ coordinates is at most $C\sqrt p (N^{-1/2}+s_M)$, where $s_M\to0$ is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$. In $d\ge5$, when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to $C(p/N+\sqrt p M^{-d})$. For fixed $p$, the sharp order is $N^{-1}+M^{-d}$ on star-containing windows and $N^{-1}$ on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.

papers.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
papers.abstract: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.

papers.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
papers.abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.

papers.title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
papers.abstract: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：为何“先连续松弛优化、再取最近离散设计”的流程会选中不利盆地，以及能否用物理可解释的手段避免这些盆地。
证据与比较：基线松弛优化在97%的运行中求解成功，但最终离散解仅约一半成功（49%）；均匀偏向刚性平坦铰链的初始化先验将成功率提升至69%，且不增加计算量、不改变优化过程；直接在外层损失惩罚 frustration 与 floppiness 提升至78%；先验所得折纸片几何兼容性与力学刚度更高。
papers.method_zh: 以自动微分做连续松弛优化，再用双层优化框架为每个折痕选择四种离散铰链类型之一；比较基线、初始化先验与外层损失惩罚三种方案。

english_guide.finding: Gradient-based relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but committed discrete solutions succeed only about half the time (49%); a uniform initialization prior toward the stiff, flat hinge raises the solve fraction to 69%, and directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss raises it to 78%.
english_guide.question: Why does the standard continuous-relaxation-then-nearest-discrete procedure select unfavorable basins, and can physically interpretable signatures of those basins be targeted to avoid them?
english_guide.evidence: Solve fractions of 97% (relaxed), 49% (baseline discrete), 69% (initialization prior), and 78% (outer-loss penalty); sheets produced with the prior show greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness.
english_guide.method: Automatic differentiation for continuous relaxation, with a bilevel optimization framework tuning which of four discrete hinge types is placed at each fold; compared against an initialization prior and an outer-loss penalty.
english_guide.novelty: The authors introduce a practical, interpretable origami-inspired design problem and show that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization; targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.
english_guide.limitations: Findings are limited to the origami model with four hinge types described in the abstract; sample conditions, experimental validation, and generality to other discrete design problems are not specified.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者提出一个实用且可解释的折纸启发设计问题，并表明损失景观中存在物理有意义但离散化不稳健的盆地，针对其物理特征（即使仅用初始化偏置）即可规避。

papers.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.

papers.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
papers.abstract: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator. We focus on the local interactions models, where the particles' states are modified only when two or more of them appear on the same grid site. The main focus is given to the two-dimensional grid in space. We study the dependence of the search algorithm asymptotic success time and probability on the interaction strength and the generated maximal entanglement between particles. We show that the interacting and non-interacting two- and three-particle search algorithm attains a constant factor improvement over the single-particle counterpart. In addition, we provide a new generalized model of interactions for multi-particle quantum walks.

papers.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.

papers.title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
papers.abstract: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

papers.title: Dynamical mean-field theory of latching Potts networks
papers.abstract: Spontaneous transitions between memories, as observed in internally generated cognition such as mind-wandering and free association, require neural dynamics capable of destabilizing one attractive memory state and moving towards another. We ask what minimal representational structure is required for such transitions to emerge in random associative networks. To address this question, we study Potts associative networks with $S$ active states per unit and slow adaptive thresholds. The $S=1$ case can model a standard Hopfield-like network of binary units. We employ dynamical mean-field theory in the extensive-load regime, where the number of stored patterns scales linearly with network size and connectivity, and we focus on transitions between two condensed memories, which are singled out in the connectivity matrix. In the finite-load regime, we show that transitions are governed by an effective drive term, whose sign and temporal evolution distinguish high-latching (structured), low-latching (random), and non-latching regimes. The resulting phase diagram shows that adaptation alone is not sufficient: transitions only occur within certain ranges of the overlap between the two memories. In the binary case $S=1$, in particular, no unit can be active in both memories but in different Potts states, thus strongly supressing the high-latching, structured transitions that exist for $S>1$. In the extensive-load regime, non-condensed memories generate colored fluctuations and retarded self-interactions through an effective memory kernel. We find that latching trajectories change the effective timescale of this kernel, a dynamical signature of transitions in the extensive-load regime. These results indicate that multi-state Potts-like representations are essential for structured memory-to-memory transitions, a hallmark of spontaneous thought.

papers.title: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
papers.abstract: In solids, the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), $Q_{μν}=g_{μν}-\frac{i}{2} Ω_{μν}$, combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Its imaginary part governs anomalous velocity and quantized Hall transport, while its real part determines the quantum weight and geometric contributions to flat-band superfluid stiffness and dielectric response. Here, we extend the QGT to four-dimensional (4D) energy-momentum space ($ω/c,k$), treating frequency and momentum as independent coordinates. Invariance of the real-spacetime plane-wave phase fixes their Lorentz transformation in energy-momentum space. Lorentz boosts of static Dirac and Weyl systems then generate frequency metrics, quadrupolar frequency-momentum shear metrics, and electric-like Berry-Maxwell fields. We identify five Lorentz-invariant contractions and derive the governing field equations and flow conservation laws for both the quantum metric and Berry curvature from static Weyl geometry and Lorentz covariance. We further connect Gaussian spectral amplitudes of the QGT to localized Gaussian events in 4D spacetime. Finally, we discuss experimental realizations in spacetime crystals or time-varying media and clarify how this unified quantum geometry of a gravitational-like metric and electromagnetic-like gauge fields connects geometric self-consistency with physical event dynamics.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于解析推导与协变构造；研究对象：固体中量子几何张量（QGT）在四维能量-动量空间（ω/c,k）的推广
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 将QGT推广到四维能量-动量空间，并由静态Dirac/Weyl系统的洛伦兹boost生成频率度规、频率-动量剪切度规及类电磁Berry-Maxwell场。

papers.title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
papers.abstract: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems: Derivation, dynamics, and spectral signatures
papers.abstract: Drive-modified dissipation in multilevel quantum systems is not, in general, accurately captured by conventional master equations. We derive a unified master equation using Lewis-Riesenfeld dynamical invariants, accommodating arbitrary driving within Born-Markov theory. We demonstrate the applicability of the unified master equation to constant-Rabi-coupling (continuous-wave), periodically-modulated-Rabi-coupling, and nonperiodic (ramped and chirped) driving protocols. Fluorescence spectra of a periodically driven three-level $Λ$ system reveal signatures missed by conventional descriptions. We trace the limitations of the conventional descriptions to inaccurate bath-frequency sampling and the neglect of nonsecular dissipative couplings, and map out the parameter regimes that require a unified treatment. The fluorescence spectra provide experimentally accessible signatures, which serve as a spectroscopic guide to reliable modeling of dissipative processes that can inform quantum control, simulation, sensing, and information processing.

papers.title: Symmetry-Controlled Criticality and Zeno Localization in a Monitored Quasiperiodic Superconductor
papers.abstract: Measurement-induced transitions of free fermions depend strongly on symmetry, but their interplay with quasiperiodic localization and superconducting pairing remains largely unexplored. We study a continuously monitored model of free fermions with pairing, where quasiperiodicity both controls localization and changes the symmetry class of the monitored field theory. Using topological entanglement entropy as a probe of nonlocal correlations in quantum state diffusion simulations, we identify a transition between a critical phase whose von Neumann entanglement entropy scales as $(\ln L)^2$ and an area-law phase, whereas no transition occurs in the clean limit, consistent with the corresponding DIII and D nonlinear sigma models. The transition line exhibits strong multifractality and depends nonmonotonically on quasiperiodicity, which we associate with the symmetry crossover. Deep in the Zeno regime, we derive an effective non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes description of individual trajectories and obtain a closed-form localization length that quantitatively agrees with numerics. Our results reveal how symmetry, quasiperiodic localization, and measurement backaction combine to determine both critical entanglement and microscopic trajectory localization in monitored superconductors.

papers.title: Discrete anomaly inflow from SymTFT of $U(1)$ global symmetry: the modified Villain resolution
papers.abstract: We construct a lattice SymTFT for a $U(1)$ global symmetry with anomaly coefficient $k$ using the modified Villain formulation, in which the spin structure required for odd $k$ is realised explicitly by lattice Majorana fermions. We demonstrate that the same Majorana fermions sit at the junctions of the symmetry lines, exactly where the fusion of two $U(1)$ elements wraps around the circle. From the lattice algebra of lines and junctions we derive the $R$- and $F$-symbols in the bulk and on the gapped boundary, and show that for odd $k$ the boundary $F$-symbol obeys the Gu-Wen relation for the $U(1)$ symmetry defect, without passing through a bosonic shadow. Restricting to $\mathbb{Z}_2\subset U(1)$, we reproduce the mod-4 anomalous phase from a mapping torus and the fermionic stacking rule. As a simple application of this SymTFT, we also determine which subgroups $\mathbb{Z}_d\subset U(1)$ can be gauged and the symmetry of the resulting theories. This is a first step towards deriving, from the anomaly inflow of a continuous symmetry, the junction data of global anomalies beyond group cohomology.

papers.title: Geometric Theory of Quasiperiodically Driven Systems
papers.abstract: Quasiperiodically driven systems give rise to a rich set of physical phenomena in contemporary quantum physics, with applications ranging from nonequilibrium dynamics to Hamiltonian engineering and control. However, unlike periodically driven (Floquet) systems, their study is hindered by the absence of a generic theory to describe their evolution using an effective time-independent Hamiltonian and its eigenstates. Based on counterdiabatic driving, we construct a general framework to identify and determine the dynamically invariant spaces of arbitrary quasiperiodic drives (i.e., the generalization of Floquet states). We decompose their unitary evolution using the exact effective average-energy operator Æ and the corresponding gauge potential, which we compute via a variational principle in frequency-lattice operator space. We then formulate a four-fold taxonomy of quasiperiodic drives based on the geometry and topology of their dynamically invariant spaces into (non)abelian and (un)twisted classes. The abelian untwisted class admits a direct extension of Floquet's theorem to incommensurate quasiperiodic drives; going beyond, we derive a nonabelian generalization of Floquet theory. Finally, we propose a concept of ergodicity whose onset is marked by coalescing dynamically invariant eigenspaces, in direct analogy to the emergence of ergodicity in a mixed classical phase space. The effective mathematical framework, variational principle, and nonabelian ergodicity we put forward apply beyond quasiperiodic drives.

papers.title: Quantum tunneling of a measurement-driven active particle
papers.abstract: Active particles can exhibit persistent motion set by their orientation. We demonstrate this key property for a quantum active particle: The particle's motion is locked to the orientation of its spin due to spin-orbit coupling and damping, and the orientation is made persistent through continuous measurement via the quantum Zeno effect. As a result, individual quantum trajectories feature an active run-and-tumble motion. When the particle impinges on a potential barrier, its persistent velocity leads to accumulation near the barrier, in contrast with the reflection of a free quantum particle. We show that quantum tunneling enhances the active particle's transmission rate compared to that of an analogous classical particle.

papers.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. Their magnitude is comparable to a circuit estimate of spontaneous emission into the electromagnetic environment. These results establish in-situ InAsSb/Al junctions as coherent, gate-tunable circuit elements and introduce cQED architecture as a microwave probe of the dynamics of the ternary weak link.

papers.title: Exact power spectra and effective dimensionality in critical block-GOE networks
papers.abstract: Criticality in neural networks is crucial for optimal information processing. Recent studies have shifted focus from static criticality to frequency-dependent behavior, particularly in oscillatory systems modeled by block-Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (block-GOE) matrices. However, analytical tools to predict spectral properties such as power spectrum and effective dimensionality remain scarce. In this work, we derive exact solutions for the network-averaged power spectrum $\operatorname{Tr}_{N}[\mathbf{S}(ω)]$, the network autocovariance $\operatorname{Tr}_{N}[\mathbf{C}(τ)]$, and the normalized effective dimensionality $D_N(ω)$ in block-GOE ensembles. These results provide a comprehensive framework for understanding how oscillatory networks operate near criticality, offering insights into the dynamic balance between stability and flexibility in large-scale neural systems.

papers.title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
papers.abstract: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane. Each point is assigned its Voronoi cell, so that the data become a landscape of prisms, and two points are linked when the line of sight between them clears the cells crossed by the connecting segment. This yields horizontal ($\HVGV$) and natural ($\NVGV$) Voronoi visibility graphs that reduce exactly to the classical horizontal and natural visibility graphs when the points are collinear, contain the Gabriel graph of the point set, and can be built by an exact walk through the Delaunay triangulation. For uncorrelated heights, the horizontal graph depends only on the ranks of the data, so its statistics are independent of the marginal distribution. The probability that two points see each other is $2/[(M+1)(M+2)]$, where $M$ is the number of Voronoi cells crossed, which reduces the problem to the geometry of the tessellation. For Poisson points this gives a degree distribution with a scale-free tail $P(k)\simeq(π^3/4)\,k^{-2}$ and a mean degree that grows as $(π^3/8)\ln N$, in contrast with the finite value $\langle k\rangle=4$ of one-dimensional series. Two dimensions are therefore the marginal case in which isotropic horizontal visibility ceases to be local. Numerical simulations with up to $N=1.28\times10^5$ points support these predictions.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论为主，数值模拟验证；提出定义并推导解析结果；研究对象：任意不规则散点采样的二维标量场，经Voronoi镶嵌构造可见性图

papers.title: Intrinsic Chiral HOTI Stabilized by a Single Diagonal Reflection
papers.abstract: Higher-order topological insulators and superconductors, under combined point and fundamental symmetries, display topological modes supported by boundaries of higher codimensions, such as a corner mode. In this work, we explain a theoretical device that enables us to claim that there exists {\it one and only one} intrinsic chiral-symmetric higher-order topological phase for the quarter-plane geometry with point-symmetry given by reflection about the diagonal of the corner. Furthermore, we supply a minimal tight-binding model of this phase and design an acoustic crystal whose dynamics reproduce that of the model. The robust properties of the corner mode are investigated by COMSOL simulations.

papers.title: Stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links hold echinocytes in a model splenic slit
papers.abstract: Stored red blood cells become echinocytes, growing spicules before losing membrane; the spleen clears the resulting small, spherical cells. Whether spicules alone hinder splenic passage is unknown. Shape and area change together. In a two-component model whose shrinking cytoskeleton raises spicules, we drove a discocyte and stage I to III echinocytes of equal area and volume through a model splenic slit. The pressure drop needed to pass rose with stage; stage III echinocytes were held at 37 to 50 times the pressure drop that passed the discocyte. Bilayer-cytoskeleton links stretched near full extension held these cells; lengthening them about twofold released a held cell. Capillary-sized channels, as in our device, separated the stages far less. Of the shape classes in stored blood, the model held at high pressure drops only storage-induced microerythrocytes, which perfused human spleens clear most. Spicules, besides membrane loss, may decide which stored cells the spleen retains.

papers.title: Proliferating against the current: how multistep branching nucleation can sort microtubule polarity in the spindle
papers.abstract: The spindle, which segregates chromosomes during cell division, is a paradigm of cytoskeletal self-organization: a highly ordered structure that persists for hours is assembled from dynamic microtubules that branch, grow, slide, and turn over within tens of seconds. Its microtubules point inward, with minus ends clustered at the poles and plus ends extending toward the chromosomes at the center of the structure. In large meiotic spindles this arrangement is puzzling, since microtubules nucleate near the chromosomes and grow at their plus ends much faster than motors slide them backward. One would therefore expect the plus ends, rather than the minus ends, to radiate outward. Here, we propose a resolution to this seeming paradox through a kinetic model that integrates the core filament-level processes. When branching complexes assemble with a sufficient delay, for instance through several sequential rate-limiting steps, they accumulate on old microtubule lattice sites near the backward-sliding minus ends of mother microtubules. Each generation is then born farther back than the last, so the self-renewing population drifts toward the minus ends even though each filament's center advances toward its plus end. For the sliding and growth velocities measured in Xenopus egg extract spindles, a multistep mechanism requires at least four rate-limiting steps. The kinetic theory has a surprisingly amenable structure: the filament length configuration variable can be eliminated exactly, yielding a finite space-time hierarchy, and the direction of population drift follows from a general criterion comparing the mean lattice age at branching sites with the ratio of plus-end advance to sliding speed.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于动力学模型与已测速度参数；研究对象：有丝分裂/减数分裂纺锤体中动态微管及其分支成核极性排序
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 多步分支成核若具足够延迟，可使自更新微管群体向负端漂移，从而解释纺锤体中负端向极聚集的极性排序。

研究问题：大型减数分裂纺锤体中微管在染色体附近成核且正端生长快于马达滑动，为何负端而非正端向外辐射？
证据与比较：摘要给出动力学模型分析：分支复合物延迟组装时在母微管负端附近旧晶格位点累积；对Xenopus卵提取物纺锤体测得的滑动与生长速度，多步机制至少需四个限速步骤；并给出消除丝长变量后的有限时空层级与群体漂移判据。

papers.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
papers.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin-valley polarization and optically tunable magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results establish 2D semiconductors as an advanced platform for integrated nonreciprocal devices, enabling functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional magneto-optical materials like all-optical operation.

papers.title: A thermodynamically consistent, fully compressible, fluctuating hydrodynamics model of a Cahn Hilliard binary fluid mixture
papers.abstract: We derive, from first principles, a thermodynamically consistent set of fully compressible fluctuating hydrodynamic equations for a Cahn-Hilliard binary fluid mixture, in isothermal and non-isothermal form and for symmetric and non-symmetric mixtures. The derivation uses the GENERIC formalism, with the friction operator constructed from flux fluctuations following Jelic and Ottinger, so that deterministic and stochastic fluxes derive from the same operator and correlation matrix and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem holds by construction. We show that the momentum equation must use the total mass density, that the Cahn-Hilliard variable is the mass fraction, and that the diffusion flux must be driven by the specific, not the volumetric, exchange potential. We derive a generalized Korteweg tensor for square-gradient energies in density and composition, and show that the reversible pressure tensor of the non-isothermal model is fixed by the degeneracy condition, producing a thermal capillary stress when the interfacial free energy has an entropic part. Thermodynamic consistency is proved in full: Jacobi identity, positivity and degeneracy, local energy conservation with interstitial-working fluxes, a local entropy balance, Soret-Dufour reciprocity, and Einstein statistics of the linearized equations. The final equations are written in conservative form for finite-volume discretization, and closed-form static and dynamic structure factors are given for all models as analytic benchmarks. An appendix shows that the same models follow from classical irreversible thermodynamics with the Helmholtz or Gibbs free energy; this route is unique for isothermal flows and has a gauge freedom in the non-isothermal case that GENERIC removes.

papers.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $ε=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=α^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.

papers.title: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
papers.abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are increasingly being integrated into cryogenic quantum-sensing platforms that operate in large magnetic fields. Here, the high-field limits of these measurements were probed by characterizing the dark count response of a NbTiN SNSPD at up to 14~T using in situ control of the detector orientation and benchmarking that performance against normal detector operation in smaller magnetic fields. The detector performance is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular magnetic fields rapidly reduce the usable bias-current range, whereas near-parallel alignment enables operation at substantially larger total fields, with a finite operating margin retained to 12~T and measurable dark-count response at the 14~T field limit. The angular dependence is governed predominantly by the perpendicular component of the magnetic field, consistent with vortex-mediated suppression of the superconducting current scale. The same field-dependent current scale also determines the electrical pulse amplitude, linking high-field detector operation directly to readout performance. These results establish a practical route for deploying SNSPDs in multi-tesla quantum-sensing and high-field cryogenic experiments.

papers.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

papers.title: What Can Next Generation Ultrafast Light Sources Tell Us About Quantum Materials?
papers.abstract: Ultrafast spectroscopy of quantum materials has emerged as a principle application of modern ultrafast optical sources. Measurements made with ultrashort pulses allow the normally strongly coupled internal degrees of freedom inside these systems to be de-coupled in the time-domain, revealing the key interactions for the different orders that lead to dramatic emergent phenomena. This has naturally motivated a wide range of experiments, and quantum materials have now been studied with ultrafast sources spanning from the hard X-ray to the THz, with fields intense enough to create non-equilibrium states, and using pulses down to the attosecond duration. As the optical spectroscopist's toolbox becomes increasingly complete, it is worth pausing and reflecting on what are the capabilities that we currently lack for examining quantum materials, and what are the problems that require the next generation of ultrafast sources now coming on-line or being designed. Here I will offer an overview of the remaining missing capabilities in ultrafast optical sources as required for studying quantum materials, and identify some outstanding problems where I believe these new sources can provide decisive impact in our understanding of quantum and strongly-correlated materials.

papers.title: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light
papers.abstract: Theoretical descriptions of the quantum electrodynamical interaction between fast electrons and nanostructures conventionally rely on standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED), which, when applied to bounded objects in vacuum, formally requires an asymptotic limiting procedure to account for free-space radiation modes. To explicitly incorporate these modes from the outset, we employ the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), which independently quantizes both the asymptotic scattering modes and the electromagnetic field generated by dissipative material sources. Utilizing an exact second-order Magnus expansion, we derive a closed-form, nonperturbative master formula for the transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange probability. In the unilluminated regime, we demonstrate that at finite nanostructure temperatures, the vacuum scattering and thermal material fluctuations do not mathematically recombine into the total imaginary part of the dyadic Green's function. This breakdown does not violate the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, because the explicit zero-temperature scattering field acts as an independent dynamical system that maintains the configuration out of global thermodynamic equilibrium. This fundamental separation reveals an intrinsic Stokes--Anti-Stokes asymmetry, yielding distinct transverse diffraction patterns for energy loss and thermal energy gain, and establishing a generalized detailed-balance relation that governs the radiative reduction of the apparent temperature in nanoscale electron thermometry. papers.title: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has continuously broadened their applicability to increasingly complex systems in chemistry and materials science. Extending MLPs to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, however, is still challenging as it requires the consideration of electrode potentials and electric fields in the atomic interactions. Such approaches have emerged only recently, and although the field is evolving rapidly, further conceptual advances are still needed for carrying out reliable simulations at finite temperature under applied potential. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview about recent progress in the atomistic simulation of electrified interfaces using MLPs. Current developments fall into three different categories. The first comprises linear response models that describe polarisation, polarisability, and Born effective charges, extending conventional MLPs to finite electric fields. The second includes methods that directly learn a field-dependent potential energy surface. The third consists of a series of hybrid approaches combining classical models with machine learning. Although still under active development, these methods represent a major step toward more realistic simulations approaching the quality of electronic structure calculations. Finally, we discuss open challenges and possible future directions for advancing MLP-based simulations aiming for a bottom-up understanding of atomistic processes at electrified interfaces.

papers.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
papers.abstract: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

papers.title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
papers.abstract: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

papers.title: Defect-induced stabilization of Wigner negativity and parity-protected phase-locking
papers.abstract: We show that a parity-preserving delta-shaped potential, mimicking the presence of a localized defect, reduces the continuous $U(1)$-symmetry of a quantum van der Pol oscillator to the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetry. This mechanism guarantees protected even-parity stationary quantum coherences, resulting in the generation of non-classical steady-states characterized by Wigner function negativity. Thanks to a non-trivial interplay between the defect and non-linear dissipative channels, this kind of negativity entails parity-protected quantum phase locking, meaning that the oscillator's energy levels simultaneously lock into two opposite phases. Finally, we present a realistic experimental proposal involving the motional state of ultracold alkaline-earth-like atoms in optical tweezers, where the localized defect is engineered via state-selective contact interactions, while the non-linear dissipative channels are driven by Raman sidebands.

papers.title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
papers.abstract: Neural scaling laws enable the prediction of returns from larger training datasets, but machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) datasets are heterogeneous and expensive to generate, and equal numbers of structures need not contain equal amounts of useful information. We study data scaling under fixed model configurations for M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined MatPES-MP-ALOE training pool. Across training structure subsets from 10,000 to 640,000, together with the full 1.16-million-structure training set, we compare uniform random sampling, three chemistry- and structure-informed stratification policies, iterative DIRECT, and furthest-point sampling using embeddings from three pretrained MLIPs. Models are evaluated using cohesive-energy, force, stress, and aggregate losses on both a held-out test set from the parent distribution and the distribution shifted MP-r$^2$SCAN test set. We observe power-law scaling improvements with increasing data, but the fitted scaling exponent, apparent error floor, and relative sample efficiency depend on the model architecture, target quantity, data sampling policy, and test set distribution. Sampling-policy rankings can reverse across test distributions: chemical stratification can improve cross-dataset performance while degrading in-distribution performance, whereas the embedding-space diversity policies frequently under-perform random sampling. Relative loss is strongly associated with test-to-train chemical-space divergence. These results show that structure count is a necessary but insufficient scaling variable for MLIPs. For training MLIPs, the return on additional first-principles calculations depends not only on how many additional structures are included, but also on how their chemical and configurational content aligns with the model's intended use.

papers.title: Quantization Breaks Classical Mpemba Constraints
papers.abstract: The Mpemba effect, in which an initially hotter system relaxes faster than a colder one, has been widely studied in both classical and quantum systems, yet identifying the specific effects of quantization requires a consistent comparison with the corresponding classical dynamics. Starting from the Caldeira-Leggett model, we establish a quantum-classical correspondence for thermal relaxation. We find that the locality of classical energy diffusion forbids the Mpemba effect in single-well and symmetric double-well potentials. Conversely, quantum dynamics allows for direct transitions between nonadjacent energy levels, overcoming the constraints of classical local energy diffusion and enabling the Mpemba effect in these potentials. In the semiclassical limit $\hbar\to0$, the nonlocal transitions become increasingly suppressed, restoring the classical constraints. Our findings reveal that quantization fundamentally unlocks anomalous relaxation pathways, rather than merely modifying relaxation rates.

papers.title: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
papers.abstract: The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems. The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables. It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

papers.title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
papers.abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

papers.title: Reducing TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits Using Solid Neon
papers.abstract: Two level systems (TLSs) are a major source of loss in superconducting devices, limiting the performance of qubits, detectors, and resonators. These defects arise from a range of sources, including surface oxides, crystal defects, as well as fabrication residues which are often difficult to remove. Using NbTiN coplanar waveguide resonators, we show that depositing and subsequently removing a solid neon film can significantly improve device performance. Analysis of the temperature and power dependence indicates that this enhancement arises from reduced TLS dissipation, which we attribute to the redistribution and removal of surface contaminants during neon deposition and evaporation. Atomic force microscopy images of contaminated hexagonal boron nitride flakes before and after neon exposure show that neon treatment can redistribute and remove surface residues. These results demonstrate a simple, non-destructive approach for mitigating TLS losses in superconducting devices and other sensitive materials that cannot withstand aggressive cleaning processes.

papers.title: A unified finite-site framework for scaffold-client biocondensation
papers.abstract: Client recruitment into biomolecular condensates does not determine how stronger binding changes the bulk free-energy advantage of demixing. Here, we use a unified finite-site thermodynamic framework to examine how scaffold-client interactions affect both the response of a fixed-composition mixture and the organization of its ternary phase diagram. The thermodynamic response to increasing client affinity is determined by the difference in heterotypic bonding between the complete equilibrium phase-separated sample and the corresponding homogeneous state. A finite region of the model exhibits positive scaffold-client concentration covariance but negative heterotypic bond contrast: stronger binding reduces the demixing advantage even when both species enrich in the dense phase. This reduction also occurs with independent scaffold self-association and client-binding site pools, without direct displacement of scaffold bonds. A negative response does not by itself imply condensate shrinkage or dissolution. Across composition space, the same finite binding constraints support scaffold-rich and heterotypic coexistence regimes with distinct bond populations. For divalent clients, these regimes can occupy disconnected regions of the phase diagram and reconnect upon increasing client affinity, depending on scaffold cohesion. Critical-point continuation identifies the folds and cusp organizing these changes, while client valence restricts the parameter range over which disconnected coexistence occurs. Explicit-particle Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the qualitative reentrant response and provide finite-size evidence for disconnected coexistence. These results provide a bond-resolved characterization of fixed-parent affinity response and a complementary description of coexistence under specified association constraints.

papers.title: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence
papers.abstract: Stabilizer measurements provide a direct route to preparing quantum error-correcting codes and long-range entangled states. In realistic implementations, however, finite measurement strength can coherently deform the encoding map away from the projective limit. Certain nonlocal signatures associated with long-range order can survive such a deformation, but this alone does not guarantee that the resulting state protects encoded quantum information. We show that, at fixed strength, local logical leakage obstructs asymptotically faithful recovery; along logical operators' supports, its accumulation forces the relevant measurement strength to grow logarithmically with code distance. We then prove that this obstruction can be removed locally: for fixed toric registers under sufficiently weak local-stochastic errors, enhancing only a vanishing fraction of checks near selected logical supports restores recovery while the bulk remains at finite measurement strength. With recoverability restored, we prove a further dimensional distinction in logical operations. In the strict three-dimensional deconfined phase, suitable enhanced tubes restore the equivalence of macroscopically separated representatives, so either representative asymptotically implements the same controlled logical action on a fixed encoding. In two dimensions, recoverability alone does not restore this equivalence: the representatives can remain inequivalent even when both associated encodings are recoverable.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论研究；基于定理证明与渐近分析；研究对象：稳定子码（stabilizer codes）与环面寄存器（toric registers）在有限测量强度下的编码

papers.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
papers.abstract: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. In an annulus surrounding a pressurized lumen, a radially aligned inner domain and a circumferentially aligned outer domain stably coexist because the domain wall is pinned at a position that results in the fibers carrying the lumen pressure. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

papers.title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. Matched training configurations and architectures enable direct comparisons with students trained on density-functional-theory (DFT) reference labels. For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance and dominant spectral features, with conductance differing by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts. In 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens loaded at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differ by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively. Exploratory SiC/a-C/SiC simulations retain the principal thermal bottleneck and the direction of the annealing response. Furthermore, a four-model committee retrieves 42-56% of the highest-error teacher configurations with a 10% selection budget and improves high-error force fitting, but does not consistently improve downstream properties. These findings demonstrate that direct distillation can preserve key interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact interatomic potentials, opening a path towards large-scale, high-throughput simulations of heterogeneous interfaces.

papers.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
papers.abstract: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

papers.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

papers.title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference weighs competing explanations of noisy data by sampling from a posterior distribution, a task that deterministic hardware performs only by simulating randomness. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) supply this randomness physically, but the few hardware networks of p-bits built so far use inorganic devices, address optimization or learning, and are judged without reference to the spread expected from finite sampling. Here we report a probabilistic computer built from solution-processed conjugated-polymer memristors. Four polymer p-bits, tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop, sample competing, degenerate and cooperative posteriors over sixteen states with statistics that fall within the range of ideal p-bits, both in their distribution and in their autocorrelation, without any parameter fitted to the target. This agreement extends to new simulated sensor readings whose outcome was predicted before each run, including readings that point away from the true answer. Reprogrammed in software, the same circuit and controller reproduces the invertible AND gate of earlier p-bit networks, with its temperature fixed in advance rather than fitted. Polymer p-bits thus open a route to printed, large-area probabilistic computers that infer alongside their sensors.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验；基于聚合物忆阻器构建概率计算机并测试采样统计；研究对象：溶液加工共轭聚合物忆阻器构成的四个概率比特（p-bits）网络
