papers.title: Thermodynamic Properties of the S=1/2 Zigzag Spin Ladder
papers.abstract: We investigate finite-temperature properties of the spin-1/2 zigzag Heisenberg ladder with an anisotropic off-diagonal $Γ$ interaction. Thermal states are calculated by an infinite time-evolving block decimation method combined with purification, while exact diagonalization is used to analyze low-lying excitations. The entropy is strongly suppressed at low temperatures inside the gapped phases, whereas it remains enhanced near several ground-state phase boundaries. For the Néel phase at $J_2/J_1=0$, the model can be mapped by spin rotations onto the exactly solvable XYZ chain. The thermal gap extracted from the low-temperature specific heat agrees with the exact one-spinon gap, while the finite-size excitation gap obtained by exact diagonalization is consistent with a two-spinon excitation.

papers.title: Hierarchical Topological Protection and Subsymmetry-Driven Edge-State Switching
papers.abstract: We reveal a hierarchy of topological protection in which multiple symmetries and their reduced forms provide distinct mechanisms for protecting topological edge states. In Hermitian Hamiltonians obtained by doubling chiral non-Hermitian systems, a structural and an inherited chiral symmetry provide complementary channels of topological protection. By selectively breaking either symmetry, we demonstrate their distinct roles in protecting edge zero modes, establishing different levels of protection under symmetry reduction. Remarkably, even when both full chiral symmetries are broken, fixed subsymmetry constraints allow the protected zero-mode configurations to switch between opposite edges and change in number across the topological phase boundaries of the symmetry-unbroken system. Our results establish a hierarchical framework for topological protection, revealing a route to controlling edge-state configurations via reduced symmetry constraints.

papers.abstract_summary_zh: 多种对称性及其约化形式构成分层拓扑保护，即使两条完整手性对称性均破缺，固定子对称性约束仍可使受保护零模在相反边缘间切换并改变数目。

证据与比较：摘要称通过选择性破缺结构手性对称性与继承手性对称性，展示二者保护边缘零模的不同角色；并指出两条完整手性对称性均破缺时，固定子对称性约束使零模在对称性未破缺系统的拓扑相边界处切换边缘并改变数目。

papers.title: Structural and electronic properties of (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ phases from first principles
papers.abstract: (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ material system is promising for ferroelectric devices, owing to their compatibility with the existing electronics manufacturing processes. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations can be used for the device design and optimization, but the predictive power of TCAD device simulations depends on the quality of the material parameters. These are still surprisingly poorly understood, also for the metastable ferroelectric phase, largely owing to the difficulties in synthesizing phase-pure samples. Here, we carry out high-quality first-principles calculations to extract reliable lattice parameters, dielectric constants, and band gaps for six of the most common phases of HfO$_2$, Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$, and ZrO$_2$. We compare results from GGA, meta-GGA, and hybrid functionals to shed light on the sensitivity of the results on the level of theory and to connect the results to earlier literature. In the case of band structures, we also consider $GW$ corrections as well as the effects of temperature-induced band gap renormalization and excitonic effects. Finally, we use these results in TCAD simulations for (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ FeCAP to demonstrate the effect that non-ferroelectric interlayers could have on the hysteresis curves and band diagrams.

papers.title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate the geometric closure of austenite--martensite interfaces. Classical compatibility conditions permit stress-free interfaces between the two phases: the condition $λ_2 = 1$ admits planar interfaces, whereas the cofactor conditions additionally admit curved interfaces. However, neither, guarantees the geometric closure of these interfaces. We identify two-parameter families of martensitic deformations that overcome this limitation and enable the formation of closed, stress-free martensite nuclei embedded in an austenite matrix. A main result is the interpretation of the classical deformation modes of simple shear and pure shear as martensitic phase transformations. These correspond to cubic to monoclinic-II and cubic to orthorhombic transformations, respectively. The former naturally satisfies the \emph{extreme compatibility conditions}, which are stronger than the cofactor conditions, and gives rise to \emph{elastic Landau states}, a self-accommodating martensitic nuclei embedded in austenite. We show that these states can be assembled to form arbitrarily shaped, stress-free martensitic islands surrounded by austenite. Such states can arise even in conventional shape memory alloys that do not satisfy supercompatibility, provided hierarchical twinning produces an average deformation that is a simple shear. The theory provides a geometric mechanism for self-accommodation. Its predicted deformation gradients agree with those reconstructed from experimentally observed microstructures. This agreement suggests that these microstructures originate from simple shear.

papers.title: Floquet first- and higher-order topological superconductors: A review
papers.abstract: The current developments in quantum technologies are deeply rooted in quantum computation, with Majorana fermions and their topological protection expected to play a central role. In this context, topological superconductors (TSCs) provide a promising platform for investigating Majorana modes and their potential applications in topological quantum computation. In dimensions $d > 1$, the spatial localization of topological Majorana modes can be controlled in higher-order topological superconductors (HOTSCs), extending beyond the conventional framework of first-order topological superconductors (FOTSCs). In this review, we systematically survey the diverse landscape of topological superconductivity, ranging from FOTSCs to third-order topological superconductors (TOTSCs), in which the spatial dimensionality of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) is progressively reduced. We demonstrate how periodic driving protocols enable Floquet engineering of all these phases, even when the corresponding undriven systems are topologically trivial. Furthermore, we investigate various driving schemes and explore the interplay among spin-orbit coupling, magnetic fields, magnetic impurities, and symmetry-breaking mass terms in realizing Floquet higher-order topological superconducting (FHOTSC) phases, characterized by appropriate topological invariants. We also provide an extensive discussion of topological invariants capable of distinguishing conventional MZMs from anomalous Majorana $pi$-modes, which emerge at two distinct quasienergies and have no static counterparts.

papers.title: Electronic Origin of Contrasting Li and Na Clustering on Graphene
papers.abstract: The electrochemical performance of anode materials is often defined by the ability of metal ions (e.g., Li and Na) to be effectively stored within the host material over a specific range of chemical potentials. This is particularly true for adsorbed Li and Na atoms on carbon surfaces (e.g., graphite or pore surfaces in hard carbon), where the interplay between ionic and metallic bonding often takes place - while metal atoms act as ionic species, in a finite concentration limit, they tend to form metallic bonding when they approach each other. What makes the case special is that, despite similar chemical identities, Li and Na atoms exhibit distinct tendencies for cluster formation; for example, the formation of Li metallic clusters on a graphene surface is only thermodynamically favorable after reaching a finite metal-ion concentration. Motivated by this, herein, we use first-principles calculations on graphene to examine the electronic origin of Li and Na clustering. Specifically, we demonstrate that the separated adsorbed atoms donate electrons to graphene, shifting the Fermi level to higher energies; however, the formation of metal clusters can result in the formation of lower-energy orbitals that are specifically associated with metal-metal bonding, thus lowering the Fermi level (and hence total energies). Importantly, while the process is somewhat similar for Na and Li atoms, the energy levels of the newly formed metallic states govern the difference in metallic cluster formation between Li and Na.

papers.title: Critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation, which remain connected after the removal of any two sites. By combining biconnected-component decomposition with the SPQR decomposition of graphs, we develop an efficient algorithm for identifying triconnected clusters in large systems. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations yield estimates of the fractal dimension $d_3=1.2308(3)$, $1.083(2)$, and $0.77(2)$ in dimensions $d=2$, $3$, and $4$, respectively, revealing a systematic decrease of $d_3$ with increasing $d$. In dimension $d=6$, the largest triconnected cluster grows logarithmically with system size, whereas on complete graphs, corresponding to $d=\infty$, it approaches a finite size. Both behaviors indicate a vanishing fractal dimension, $d_3=0$, for $d\geq6$. Furthermore, the singular contribution to the susceptibility-like quantity associated with the second moment of the triconnected-cluster size distribution scales as $χ\sim L^{2d_3-d}$. Consequently, it vanishes for $d\geq3$, leaving a finite asymptotic susceptibility, in contrast to the divergent behavior observed in standard percolation.

papers.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
papers.abstract: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

papers.title: Plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion: Electron-hole asymmetry of the effective interlayer tunneling
papers.abstract: The effective interlayer tunneling (EIT) is a key quantity in determining the out-of-phase plasmons of a bilayer structure. Using the tight-binding model and the random phase approximation, we investigate plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion. Both O/O and G/O bilayers exhibit strong electron-hole asymmetry in the EIT. For the O/O bilayer, the gap of the out-of-phase plasmon remains almost constant as the electron concentration varies, whereas it increases rapidly with increasing hole concentration; hole doping can also lead to stronger anomalous dispersion than electron doping. For the G/O bilayer, enhancing the Kekulé distortion $Δ_0$ can weaken the EIT, as reflected by the reduced interlayer hybridization caused by the lifted layer degeneracy, especially for the electron-doped case. For the electron-doped G/O bilayer, the EIT is almost turned off when $Δ_0=0.3$ from the perspective of the dispersion. Our results imply that switching the doping type between electron and hole can tune the performance of out-of-phase plasmon-based devices by modulating the EIT.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论计算；基于紧束缚模型与随机相近似；研究对象：含O型Kekulé畸变（O-type Kekulé distortion）的双层石墨烯，包括O/O与G/O构型
papers.abstract_summary_zh: O/O与G/O双层均表现出有效层间隧穿（EIT）的强电子-空穴不对称性，使反相等离激元的色散与能隙随掺杂类型显著不同。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：O型Kekulé畸变如何影响双层石墨烯的有效层间隧穿，并由此改变反相等离激元的色散与能隙？
证据与比较：摘要给出：O/O双层反相等离激元能隙随电子浓度变化近乎不变，随空穴浓度快速增大；空穴掺杂的反常色散强于电子掺杂；G/O双层中增大Δ0削弱EIT，电子掺杂下Δ0=0.3时色散上EIT近乎关闭。
papers.method_zh: 采用紧束缚模型（tight-binding model）与随机相近似（random phase approximation）计算双层石墨烯的等离激元。

english_guide.finding: Both O/O and G/O bilayers show strong electron-hole asymmetry in the effective interlayer tunneling (EIT); for O/O the out-of-phase plasmon gap is nearly constant with electron concentration but increases rapidly with hole concentration, and hole doping gives stronger anomalous dispersion.
english_guide.question: How does O-type Kekulé distortion affect the effective interlayer tunneling and thereby the out-of-phase plasmons in bilayer graphene?
english_guide.evidence: The O/O gap stays almost constant versus electron concentration but grows rapidly with hole concentration; hole doping yields stronger anomalous dispersion. In G/O, increasing Δ0 weakens EIT, and for electron-doped G/O the EIT is almost turned off at Δ0=0.3 from the dispersion perspective.

papers.title: Emergent Quantized Zak Phases without Dimerization in a Multicomponent Fermionic Extended Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Quantized Zak phases are commonly associated with dimerized systems, such as the noninteracting Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model. In interacting systems, however, interactions can induce effective dimerization of particle clusters even in the absence of explicit dimerization in the underlying lattice. In this work, we study a one-dimensional multicomponent fermionic extended Hubbard model under a resonance condition between the on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions. We find that quantized Zak phases emerge for odd fermion numbers $n\geqslant 3$, protected by the inversion symmetry of the effective Hamiltonian. Furthermore, in the presence of a tilted field, fermion clusters exhibit Bloch oscillations, during which their Zak phases can be extracted from the evolution of a Gaussian wave packet over one Bloch period. Our results reveal an interaction-induced mechanism for realizing quantized Zak phases in multicomponent fermionic systems without explicit lattice dimerization.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论计算；依据为模型哈密顿量与有效哈密顿量分析；研究对象：一维多组分费米子扩展Hubbard模型，在位与最近邻相互作用满足共振条件
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在无显式二聚化的多组分费米子扩展Hubbard模型中，奇数费米子数n≥3时可出现量子化Zak相位，并由有效哈密顿量的反演对称性保护。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：能否在不含显式晶格二聚化的相互作用多组分费米子体系中实现量子化Zak相位，以及其保护机制与探测方式为何。
证据与比较：摘要报告：在共振条件下，奇数n≥3出现量子化Zak相位；倾斜场下费米子团簇发生Bloch振荡，可由高斯波包在一个Bloch周期内的演化提取Zak相位。摘要未给出具体数值或参数范围。
papers.method_zh: 研究一维多组分费米子扩展Hubbard模型，在共振条件下构造有效哈密顿量并分析反演对称性；另考察倾斜场下的Bloch振荡与高斯波包演化。

english_guide.question: Can quantized Zak phases arise in an interacting multicomponent fermionic system without explicit dimerization, and what protects and probes them?
english_guide.evidence: The abstract reports quantized Zak phases for odd n≥3 under a resonance condition and extraction from Gaussian wave-packet evolution over one Bloch period under a tilted field; no quantitative values are given.
english_guide.method: Study of a one-dimensional multicomponent fermionic extended Hubbard model under an on-site/nearest-neighbor interaction resonance, effective Hamiltonian and inversion-symmetry analysis, and tilted-field Bloch oscillations.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state an interaction-induced mechanism for realizing quantized Zak phases in multicomponent fermionic systems without explicit lattice dimerization.
english_guide.limitations: Conditions are the interaction resonance and odd fermion number n≥3; the abstract does not specify parameter ranges, finite-size effects, or experimental feasibility.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian limit distributions of giant-component sizes in inhomogeneous networks
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the size distribution of giant components in percolation and epidemic spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit. Instead, when appropriately scaled, the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD). This scaling behavior aligns with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT), which governs sums of random variables following heavy-tailed distributions. For scale-free networks, the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent of the network, independently of the control parameter. In contrast, on the Farey graph, a deterministic hierarchical small-world network, the scaling exponent varies continuously with the control parameter.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论分析；基于渗流与传播模型及极限定理推导；研究对象：高度非均匀网络中的巨组分，包括无标度网络与Farey图
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 高度非均匀网络上巨组分尺寸分布在热力学极限下常不收敛于高斯分布，适当标度后收敛于非高斯极限分布（NGLD）。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：渗流与传染病传播模型中巨组分尺寸的涨落分布在热力学极限下服从何种极限分布，以及标度指数由什么决定。
证据与比较：摘要给出两类网络的对比：无标度网络上标度指数仅由度指数决定、与控制参数无关；Farey图上标度指数随控制参数连续变化。未提供具体数值或模拟数据。
papers.method_zh: 将巨组分尺寸分布与广义中心极限定理（GCLT）对照，分析重尾随机变量求和的标度行为。

english_guide.finding: The size distribution of giant components on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit; when appropriately scaled, it converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD).
english_guide.question: What limit distribution governs giant-component size fluctuations in percolation and epidemic spreading models in the thermodynamic limit, and what determines the scaling exponent?
english_guide.evidence: The abstract contrasts scale-free networks, where the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent independently of the control parameter, with the Farey graph, where the exponent varies continuously with the control parameter; no numerical values are given.
english_guide.method: Comparison of giant-component size distributions with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT) for sums of heavy-tailed random variables.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state that the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD) rather than a Gaussian, with scaling behavior aligned with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT).
english_guide.limitations: Conclusions are restricted to percolation and spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks; finite-size effects, network size ranges, and numerical validation details are not specified in the abstract.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称巨组分尺寸分布不收敛于高斯分布，而收敛于非高斯极限分布（NGLD），且其标度行为符合广义中心极限定理（GCLT）。

papers.title: Stochastic evolution of interacting directed strings
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic dynamics of a system of $N$ polymer rings on an infinite cylinder with only excluded volume interaction, using simulations and also analytically. The strings can diffuse in the transverse direction by local Rouse-like moves where an up-kink changes to a down -kink, or vice versa. The motion is biased if the rates of flip are not equal. In the initial state, we start with a step initial condition: all the sites with a positive $y$ coordinate are empty, and the sites with $y \leq 0$ are occupied with a uniform density. We study the scaling form of the density profile in the hydrodynamic limit. The scaling form is a function of $y/\sqrt{t}$ in the unbiased case, and a function of $y/t$ in the biased case. In the unbiased case, in the steady state on a torus, the marginal probability distribution of the positions of the strings on a line with fixed $x$-coordinate is exactly same as that in the ground state of quantum-mechanical spin-less fermions on a line. The biased problem is equivalent to a growing surface in $2+1$ dimension, which is expected to be in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论与计算模拟结合；摘要称使用模拟并辅以解析；研究对象：无限圆柱面上仅含排除体积相互作用的N个聚合物环（polymer rings）体系
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 密度分布在无偏情形按y/√t标度、有偏情形按y/t标度；无偏稳态的边际分布与一维无自旋费米子基态相同，有偏问题对应2+1维KPZ生长表面。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：该聚合物环体系在阶跃初始条件下，密度分布如何随时间和空间标度，以及偏置翻转速率如何改变标度行为。
证据与比较：摘要给出阶跃初始条件：y>0为空、y≤0以均匀密度占据；报告无偏情形标度变量为y/√t、有偏情形为y/t；并指出环面稳态下固定x坐标线上位置的边际概率分布与一维无自旋费米子基态精确相同。
papers.method_zh: 模拟与解析结合；采用局部Rouse类移动，即上扭结（up-kink）转为下扭结（down-kink）或反之，并比较翻转速率相等与不等的情形。

english_guide.finding: Density profiles scale as y/√t without bias and y/t with bias; the unbiased steady-state marginal distribution on a fixed-x line equals that of ground-state spinless fermions, and the biased problem maps to a 2+1D KPZ growing surface.
english_guide.question: How does the density profile of interacting directed polymer rings evolve from a step initial condition, and how does biased kink flipping change the scaling?
english_guide.evidence: Step initial condition: y>0 empty, y≤0 uniformly occupied. Scaling variables y/√t (unbiased) and y/t (biased) are reported; the unbiased torus steady-state marginal distribution is exactly that of one-dimensional spinless fermions.
english_guide.method: Simulations and analytics using local Rouse-like moves in which an up-kink changes to a down-kink or vice versa, comparing equal and unequal flip rates.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state an exact correspondence of the unbiased steady-state marginal distribution with ground-state spinless fermions and an equivalence of the biased problem to a 2+1D KPZ growing surface.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract specifies only the step initial condition and infinite-cylinder/torus setting; N, density, flip rates, and finite-size or finite-time corrections are not given.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者在摘要中提出：无偏稳态边际分布与一维无自旋费米子基态精确对应，有偏问题等价于2+1维KPZ生长表面。

papers.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：计算：晶体结构预测与机器学习势分子动力学；研究对象：混合阴离子锂氧氯化物 Li_yMO_xCl_{6-2x}（M = Nb、Ta、Ti、Zr、Hf）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 氧含量升高使富氯孤立多面体依次转变为链状及更高连接度的二维、三维骨架，并由此调控锂离子输运。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：氧含量、结构骨架与锂离子输运之间的关系尚不明确，需厘清阴离子组成如何决定骨架与扩散行为。
证据与比较：在 Group 5 系列中，x≈0.67–1.5 区间出现快锂扩散，Li 位点构成三维逾渗网络；平均力势图与 nudged elastic band 计算显示快输运需低维骨架、低配位 Li 位点低势垒及位点能量相近；精细网格组分搜索给出四个稳定候选，预测室温自扩散系数最高约 10^-6 cm^2/s。
papers.method_zh: 晶体结构预测、机器学习原子间势分子动力学、平均力势图与 nudged elastic band 计算、精细网格组分搜索。

english_guide.finding: Increasing oxygen content transforms isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and then more connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks, governing Li-ion transport.
english_guide.question: How oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport are related in mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides remains unclear.
english_guide.evidence: In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over x ≈ 0.67–1.5 with a three-dimensional percolating Li-site network; potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations indicate low-dimensional frameworks, undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, and similar site energies; fine-grid search identifies four stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities up to ~10^-6 cm^2/s.

papers.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion
papers.abstract: We use the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits. For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, we express the chiral-symmetric Lax operator along a periodic orbit in a frequency basis. Energy conservation makes both bands of the resulting tight-binding model exactly flat. The harmonic oscillator corresponds to a fully dimerized topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while nonlinearity generates long-range hopping through higher harmonics. In the symmetric double well, the winding number changes as intrawell periodic orbits give way to an orbit spanning both wells, and the zero-energy edge mode of the semi-infinite chain disappears. We derive the edge-mode profile and show that its localization length diverges logarithmically as the separatrix is approached. At the separatrix, the period and the hopping decay length diverge while the band gap remains finite; this singular limit of the periodic motion allows the winding number of the infinite frequency chain to change. Canonical quantization of the Lax operator also connects the chiral winding numbers to supersymmetric quantum mechanics: for a bound system on the real line with simple turning points, their sum over all periodic orbits at a common positive energy equals the Witten index. We also apply the construction to periodic nonlinear waves through traveling-wave reductions. The finite-period winding number becomes undefined in their solitary-wave limits.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；基于经典可积系统Lax表述与紧束缚模型分析；研究对象：一维哈密顿系统（谐振子、对称双势阱）及周期非线性波
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 经典非线性周期轨道的Lax算符可映射为手征对称紧束缚模型，其能带严格平坦，且绕数在分界线处发生改变。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：如何用经典可积系统的Lax表述刻画非线性周期轨道的拓扑性质，并建立与量子模型的联系？
证据与比较：谐振子对应完全二聚化SSH模型；非线性产生高次谐波长程跃迁；双势阱中内阱轨道让位于跨阱轨道时绕数改变，半无限链零能边缘模消失；边缘模局域长度随趋近分界线对数发散；分界线处周期与跃迁衰减长度发散而带隙有限。
papers.method_zh: 采用经典可积系统的Lax表述，在频率基下表示手征对称Lax算符，构建紧束缚模型并计算绕数、边缘模及正则量子化。

english_guide.finding: The Lax operator along classical nonlinear periodic orbits maps to a chiral-symmetric tight-binding model with exactly flat bands; the winding number changes at the separatrix and the zero-energy edge mode disappears.
english_guide.question: How to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits using the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems and connect it to quantum models?
english_guide.evidence: Harmonic oscillator corresponds to fully dimerized SSH model; nonlinearity generates long-range hopping via higher harmonics; in symmetric double well, winding number changes as intrawell orbits give way to a spanning orbit; edge-mode localization length diverges logarithmically near separatrix; at separatrix period and hopping decay length diverge while band gap remains finite.
english_guide.method: Lax formulation of classical integrable systems; express chiral-symmetric Lax operator in frequency basis; construct tight-binding model; compute winding number, edge modes, and canonical quantization.
english_guide.novelty: Authors claim connection between topology of classical nonlinear periodic orbits and tight-binding models, SSH model, and Witten index in supersymmetric quantum mechanics.
english_guide.limitations: Abstract does not specify applicability conditions; only one-degree-of-freedom systems and traveling-wave reductions of periodic nonlinear waves are considered; no experimental verification or material parameters provided.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者声称将经典非线性周期轨道的拓扑与紧束缚模型、SSH模型及超对称量子力学中的Witten指数相联系。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明适用条件；仅涉及一维单自由度系统及周期非线性波的行波约化，未提供实验验证或具体材料参数。

papers.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
papers.abstract: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：实验；基于超导自旋开关的输运测量；研究对象：GdN/Nb/RuO2三明治结构中的Nb/RuO2埋藏界面
papers.abstract_summary_zh: Nb/RuO2界面存在隐藏磁性亚系统，作者归因于Nb夺取RuO2氧形成的薄RuOx氧化还原层，该层表现为弱且磁硬的铁磁体，并具空位诱导各向异性。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：RuO2表面与界面弱静磁性的来源、稳定机制及其与界面态的联系尚不明确，本文探究Nb/RuO2界面是否存在隐藏磁性及其成因。
证据与比较：GdN/Nb/RuO2三层结构的超导转变温度随界面交换场取向可调，呈现自旋开关行为；超电流增强开关效率，使探针灵敏度可原位调节。摘要未给出具体转变温度数值或磁化强度定量结果。
papers.method_zh: 制备GdN/Nb/RuO2三层超导自旋开关，通过界面交换场取向调控Nb超导转变温度，探测常规磁强计无法触及的界面磁性。

english_guide.finding: A hidden magnetic subsystem emerges at the Nb/RuO2 interface, attributed to a thin RuOx redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO2; this layer behaves as a weak, magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy.
english_guide.question: Where interfacial magnetism in RuO2 resides, what stabilizes it, and whether it connects to surface/interface states remain open; this work probes hidden magnetism at the Nb/RuO2 interface.
english_guide.evidence: The GdN/Nb/RuO2 trilayer shows a superconducting spin-switch behavior: interfacial exchange-field alignment tunes the Nb superconducting transition temperature. papers.title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-André critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.

papers.title: Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$
papers.abstract: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

papers.title: A new representation of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic potentials through stochastic duality
papers.abstract: We revisit the classical problem of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic force fields by combining homogenization with stochastic duality. We consider a specific class of fluctuations in which the internal state of the force field is independently redrawn from a fixed distribution at Poisson-distributed times. In the homogenization framework, the effective diffusion coefficient \(D_{\rm eff}\) is expressed in terms of a corrector function satisfying a backward Kolmogorov equation. For the redraw dynamics considered here, the equation governing the spatial derivative of the corrector can be reinterpreted as the stationary forward equation of a dual system obtained by reversing the force field, \(F\to-F\). This relation eliminates the corrector and yields a representation of \(D_{\rm eff}\) entirely in terms of stationary densities and probability currents of the physical and dual systems. We further introduce an auxiliary function \(Q(x)\) whose spatial variation is determined by the stationary current. When this current vanishes, \(Q(x)\) becomes independent of position and the effective diffusion coefficient reduces to the local relation \( D_{\rm eff}=L^2Q. \) This result generalizes the classical Lifson--Jackson relation to fluctuating periodic force fields. We verify the theory using analytical calculations, numerical solutions of the stationary equations, and direct simulations of the long-time particle displacement, including a driven system with nonzero stationary current.

papers.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators
papers.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.

papers.title: Facilitated Relaxation Overrides Energetic Pathways in a Multiphase Square-Kagome Artificial Spin Ice
papers.abstract: Relaxation in interacting many-body systems is typically assumed to follow energy minimization, yet local dynamical rules can determine which microscopic pathways are accessible. In facilitated relaxation, these pathways are enabled or blocked by neighboring configurations. However, isolating such rules in natural materials is difficult because energetics, disorder and dynamics are usually entangled. Here we realize a geometrically tunable square-kagome artificial spin ice-a lithographic nanomagnet array-that provides a clean, designable platform for facilitated relaxation. The array hosts two tunable nearest-neighbor interactions and supports multiple low-energy phases: spin crystal, spin liquid and spin foam. In the spin-foam phase, abundant facilitator configurations allow relaxation to follow Boltzmann statistics. In the spin-crystal phase, by contrast, domain-wall excitations are trapped in non-Boltzmann distributions, although energetically preferred relaxation channels exist. The ordered crystal background lacks the facilitators needed to connect topologically distinct domain-wall classes. These classes are therefore kinetically isolated, as observed in both experiment and Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that transition-network topology can override energetic relaxation, establishing artificial spin ice as a programmable platform for constrained dynamics and nonergodic relaxation.

papers.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
papers.abstract: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $π$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.

papers.title: TASCopilot: A provenance-preserving assistant for triple-axis neutron scattering
papers.abstract: Experimental decisions often depend on evidence scattered across papers, instrument logs, data files, and specialist software. A scientific assistant must connect that evidence without turning a plausible interpretation into an unsupported conclusion. TAS Co-pilot addresses this problem for triple-axis spectroscopy (TAS), which uses neutrons to probe material structure and excitations. It preserves provenance: the sources, processing steps, and review decisions behind each result. Independently maintained scientific tools communicate through structured requests and results; validation rules and human review govern how evidence can support a claim. Language models extract information and explain outcomes but do not approve scientific claims or control the instrument. Dependency-aware reduction executes existing scientific routines and reuses unchanged intermediate results. A retrospective SrMn$_2$Sb$_2$ study connects literature on a related material and historical alignment records to modeling of magnetic excitations in 20 measured scans. A live BT-7 study uses a dedicated instrument interface for fine alignment and 40 adaptively selected measurements. Agreement with a conventional measurement of the same crystal at shared conditions supports the acquisition and analysis chain. These cases demonstrate a methodology for maintaining inspectable evidence across literature, numerical analysis, and measurement at a user facility.

papers.title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
papers.abstract: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. We simultaneously measure photodynamics at the Re O$_{2}$ and Se M$_{4,5}$ edges, enabling decomposition of excited-state dynamics into the contributions of electron, hole, band gap, and phonon dynamics occurring around Re and Se atoms. By correlating spectral features at the Re and Se edges, we infer the existence of flat conduction bands and identify hot hole transfer from Re to Se atoms. We observe phonon oscillations driven by hole-mediated displacive excitations. The measurements highlight that the photodynamics are dominated by charge transfer between metallic sites which drives phonon coupling in the nonequilibrium state. This work provides insights into the optoelectronic applications of superatomic crystals for future tuning of emergent material properties.

papers.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
papers.abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

papers.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
papers.abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $μ$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $μ$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $μ$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $μ$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.

papers.title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
papers.abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.

papers.title: Hybridization-brightened interlayer excitons in multilayer WSe2 controlled by sliding ferroelectricity
papers.abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) combine spatially separated electron and hole wavefunctions with electrically tunable dipole moments, but their reduced wavefunction overlap generally limits optical emission, particularly for high-energy states. Here we report a bright, spectrally narrow high-energy interlayer exciton (h-IX) near 2.23 eV in few-layer WSe2 and investigate how its optical activity evolves with layer number and sliding-ferroelectric polarization. In pristine 2H-WSe2, we observe thickness-dependent brightening of high-energy exciton emission. GW-BSE calculations reveal mixed intralayer and interlayer configurations with enhanced optical weight, suggesting that multilayer hybridization contributes to the observed brightening. In parallel-stacked 3L/3L WSe2 containing a sliding-ferroelectric interface, the h-IX exhibits polarization-dependent energies and Stark responses that distinguish Pup and Pdown domains. Electric-field-driven domain-wall motion produces hysteretic transfer of spectral weight between the two h-IX branches, enabling optical tracking of ferroelectric switching. These results establish multilayer hybridization as a route to optically active high-energy interlayer excitons and sliding ferroelectricity as a complementary degree of freedom for controlling their energy, dipole and emission.

papers.title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
papers.abstract: In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.

papers.title: Study of the frustrated SU(3) Heisenberg chain with SU(3)-symmetric matrix product states
papers.abstract: We study the SU(3) Heisenberg chain with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange $J_1$ and $J_2$. Field theory predicts that the trimerized valence-bond solid of this chain has a finite extent in $α=J_2/J_1$, followed by a gapless SU(3)$_1$ phase, but earlier numerical estimates of the upper boundary range from $α\approx2.1$ (exact diagonalization) to $α\approx3.8$ (iDMRG). We use the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm with the full non-Abelian SU(3) symmetry imposed on the virtual bonds, reaching bond dimensions up to $D\approx8000$, and locate the phase boundaries by finite-entanglement scaling. Resolving the transfer-matrix spectrum and the entanglement spectrum by SU(3) irreducible representation, we find that the trimerized phase extends to $α_{c2}\gtrsim3.5$ and end below $α\approx5$, excluding a boundary near $α\approx2$. At larger $α$ our numerical analysis of the effective central charge is consistent with the predicted massless flow from SU(3)$_2$ to SU(3)$_1$.

papers.title: Mimicking the zero-field Josephson diode effect with remanent magnetization and self-field
papers.abstract: A Josephson junction whose critical current is larger in one direction than in the other is a diode. With a magnetized barrier, a junction can be a diode at zero applied field, and this is commonly attributed to an intrinsic Josephson diode effect, in which the magnetic barrier breaks time-reversal symmetry. Here we show that the same signatures arise from two ordinary ingredients: the magnetic field of the bias current in the electrodes and the remanent magnetization of the barrier. In cross-type Nb/Pd$_{89}$Ni$_{11}$/Nb junctions, the self-field displaces the interference patterns of the two current polarities in opposite directions. An in-plane remanent magnetization translates the pattern and brings the resulting asymmetry to zero field, where the junction mimics a nonvolatile diode with an asymmetry of 10 to 12% and a polarity set by the magnetization direction. Reversing the current or the field cannot distinguish this mimic from an intrinsic effect, but the wiring can: moving the current lead to the other arm of the electrode across the field reverses the self-field diode, in applied field and at zero field alike, whereas an intrinsic diode would be unchanged. This gives a simple dc test for Josephson diodes in the current-perpendicular-to-plane geometry.

papers.title: After equilibration
papers.abstract: `Complexity' measures the exploration of state space by the dynamics at a finer level of detail than that required for the equilibration of standard extensive observables , and therefore continues to grow long after these observables have equilibrated. In a recent paper, we proposed that this exploration may be quantified by the large deviations attained over time, or, equivalently, by the time taken for `rare' observables -- such as, for example the exponential of the magnetization -- to equilibrate. It turns out that the evolution of complexity can then be naturally mapped onto a standard model of glassy dynamics, the "Trap Model" , which exhibits aging and effective temperatures. Under this mapping, the exploration of increasingly fine details of phase-space corresponds to the discovery of progressively deeper minima in the glassy model.

papers.title: Dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
papers.abstract: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on Rényi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for Rényi-2. Focusing on Rényi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ansätze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher Rényi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of Rényi evolution in deterministic systems.

papers.title: Quantum Control Geometry as a Metric of Chaos
papers.abstract: Quantum-chaotic systems share the same coarse-grained features characteristic of random matrices, such as Wigner-Dyson level-spacing statistics, yet can exhibit strikingly different eigenstate structure and many-body dynamics, including relaxation, transport, scrambling, and entanglement growth. This raises the fundamental question of whether these finer-grained features probe genuinely distinct aspects of quantum chaos or, instead, reflect different manifestations of a common underlying structure---and whether such structure provides a meaningful basis for regarding one many-body quantum system as "more chaotic" than another. Here, we address this question by introducing a quantum geometric framework that quantifies the susceptibility of many-body eigenstates to physically allowed deformations of the Hamiltonian, as constrained by spatial locality, symmetries, and conservation laws. The resulting geometric susceptibility is quantitative, providing a metric of chaos beyond traditional binary diagnostics; intrinsic, as it depends on the manifold of allowed Hamiltonian deformations rather than on the way the system is probed; and unifying, as it directly connects eigenstate structure with dynamics. For canonical models of quantum chaos, we find that minimal geometric susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad spectral response of local operators, and the suppression of nonhydrodynamic slow structure coalesce in the same region of Hamiltonian control space. This suggests that these seemingly distinct signatures of chaos are different manifestations of a common underlying geometric structure. Our framework provides a route toward understanding the limits of relaxation and scrambling under physical constraints; in applications, it offers a means to engineer strongly chaotic regimes in programmable quantum systems with restricted controls.

papers.title: Chiral Superconductivity Indifferent to Parent Topology in the Square-Lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: We study a $π$-flux square-lattice $t$-$t'$ Hofstadter-Hubbard model proposed to be realizable in twisted moiré bilayers. By tuning $U$ and $t'$ at half filling, ground-state density-matrix renormalization group simulations (DMRG) and a parton analysis identify an integer quantum Hall (IQH) phase, a chiral spin liquid (CSL), and an antiferromagnet (AFM) in the phase diagram, while charge and spin fluctuations from finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) suggest a closing charge gap but an open spin gap at the IQH-CSL boundary, consistent with the topological criticality expected there. This model therefore produces a phase diagram hosting weakly correlated band topology (IQH), intrinsic topological order (CSL), and conventional symmetry breaking (AFM) side by side. Upon doping any of these three parent phases, a single chiral topological superconductor with spin Chern number $C_s=-2$ occupies nearly the entire phase diagram. DMRG, DQMC, and weak-coupling perturbation theory agree on its pairing symmetry. This shows that doping the topological band of our model robustly induces the same paired state throughout the phase diagram regardless of the character of the underlying correlated half-filled state and its magnetic fluctuations, whether an IQH, a spin liquid or a weakly fluctuating AFM.

papers.title: Planckian Charge Equilibration in Fast Scramblers
papers.abstract: The Planckian time, $τ_{\rm Pl}=\hbar/(k_BT)$, is conjectured to set a lower limit on thermal relaxation times in strongly interacting quantum matter. Rigorous bounds limit both how rapidly quantum information can scramble and how soon hydrodynamics can emerge, yet the relation between the scrambling and equilibration rates remains unclear. We address this question by studying the relaxation of a charge imbalance between two subsystems of the complex Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model and its Yukawa generalizations, which exhibit maximal scrambling. In the low-temperature conformal regime, we find through a linear response analysis that the slowest decay of this imbalance occurs at rate $Γ=2π(2Δ-d)k_BT/\hbar$, where $Δ$ is the fermion scaling dimension and $d=0,1$ is the spatial dimension. These results establish Planckian charge equilibration in maximally scrambling systems and show that maximal scrambling alone does not fix its dimensionless prefactor.

papers.title: Hidden Spin-Supercurrent Counterflow in Conventional Superconductors
papers.abstract: Resistive spin currents conventionally vary in space through spin relaxation or torque, which removes angular momentum from the transported spin. We here demonstrate a qualitatively different mechanism in a conventional superconductor exposed to a spin-splitting field. Spin injection across a spin-mixing interface activates a spin-supercurrent contribution, allowing the resistive spin current to vary spatially while the total spin current remains conserved. Even without a net spin-bias across the superconductor, finite and oppositely directed resistive and condensate spin currents arise. This produces a hidden spin-supercurrent counterflow with vanishing total spin and charge currents. The mechanism persists away from exact compensation and remains sizable over broad parameter ranges. The counterflow may be accessible through spin-to-charge conversion, either as a modification of the electrical response of spin-Hall injectors or through a local quasiparticle inverse spin-Hall signal. Our results establish condensate-mediated spin-current compensation as a previously overlooked alternative to spin relaxation.

papers.title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
papers.abstract: Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.

papers.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
papers.abstract: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.

papers.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization charge-induced modification of Schottky barrier width strongly affects the hole transport and memory properties of MoS2-HZO FeFETs. We further demonstrate several advantages and unique features of the FeFETs such as nondestructive data readout, non-volatile data retention under zero gate bias, low operation voltage, high write endurance and ultra-fast switching speed. These 1T memory cells can simplify the dense 3D integrated array architecture and offer additional practical functionalities, such as fast programming and erasing of large data arrays that are absent for many conventional memories. The demonstrated MoS2 and HZO-based FeFET shows great potential for on-chip complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible circuits for multifunctional devices, especially for 3D monolithically integrated architectures for AI workload.

papers.title: Borrowed Planckian dissipation in magic-angle twisted graphene
papers.abstract: In strange metals, the ratio of the coefficients producing signature linear-in-$T$ resistivity and the logarithmic specific heat is free of the coupling between the electrons and whatever scatters them. In the materials studied so far that coupling is fixed by chemistry. Magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene provides a dial with a displacement field $D$ that breaks the mirror symmetry separating a light Dirac cone from the flat bands, and the Dirac carriers borrow the Planckian self-energy of the flat band with a weight proportional to $D^2+D_0^2$. Resistance curves taken at eight fields are consistent with the field acting on the scattering rate rather than on the number of carriers. The slope in temperature follows $a(1+D^2/D_0^2)$ without the quartic term that a depleting Dirac pocket adds, and the elastic part varies by less than 5\% between 0.20 and 0.30~V/nm while the inelastic part grows 2.5-fold up to 0.38~V/nm. The thermally averaged Kubo formula favors flat-band weight placed symmetrically about the Fermi level over a single level. Borrowed dissipation keeps the bath exponent and transport prefactor of the flat band's own electrons but carries exactly twice their entropy per unit of borrowed coupling whenever the bath has dynamics of its own, so the field-differential ratio is $2π^3/21ζ(3)\approx2.46$ for a conformal flat band and, in a numerical search, at most 2.73 for monotonic bath spectra without a high-energy rate floor. The discriminating test is the entropy measured in steps of $D$.

papers.title: Goldstone-Mediated Chiral Superconductivity in Self-Doped Electron Crystals
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene in the proximity of electronic crystalline phases, we study the possibility of pairing mediated by electronic phonons. We focus on the vicinity of the phase boundary between trivial and topological electron crystals, where self-doping generically gives rise to a small Fermi sea of carriers with Dirac dispersion. We compute the Goldstone phonon spectra of the self-doped crystal (SDC) using a self-consistent approach, and subsequently derive the effective electronic-phonon-mediated interaction between itinerant carriers at the Fermi surface. Remarkably, we find that the Coulomb repulsion can be overscreened by the Goldstone phonons, leading to a chiral topological superconductor with an unpaired Majorana edge mode. Our conclusions are robust across the $λ$-jellium model and a simplified model of rhombohedral graphene, and we propose characteristic non-linear I-V signals as a test of our prediction. More generally, our results outline an intriguing route for unconventional superconductivity where both electronic correlations and topology play key roles.

papers.title: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov transition and quantum criticality in polarized Fermi gases
papers.abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature transition from the polarized normal phase to the FFLO state in a two-dimensional Fermi gas by means of a diagrammatic t-matrix approach. We first show that the standard non-self-consistent theory produces an unphysical critical polarization because of a severe violation of the Luttinger theorem. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a minimal self-consistent extension that largely restores compliance with the Luttinger theorem while preserving the analytical simplicity of the original formalism. This leads to a physically consistent critical polarization over the whole interaction range. Building on this improved description, we characterize the quantum critical behavior of the FFLO transition through the quasiparticle decay rates, quasiparticle weights, momentum distributions, and the critical dynamics of both fermionic and bosonic degrees of freedom. We further compare the two- and three-dimensional systems, showing that their critical properties can be understood within a unified geometrical picture based on the nesting of the majority and minority Fermi surfaces. Finally, for a three-dimensional lattice, we demonstrate within the Hertz-Millis framework that vertex corrections are irrelevant, thereby placing the FFLO quantum phase transition in the mean-field universality class, in close analogy with the itinerant antiferromagnet transition.

papers.title: Excess charge in the Engel-Dreizler model of atoms and molecules
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit excess-charge bound for the exchange-free Engel--Dreizler functional of atoms and molecules. If $αλ\le1/1233$ and $α^3Z_k^2\le1/137$ for each nucleus, every finite-mass electronic minimizer whose total energy, including nuclear repulsion, is nonpositive satisfies $N-\sum_kZ_k<(5913/1000)λ^{3/2}K$. For the gradient coefficient $λ=1/9$, this gives $N-\sum_kZ_k<0.219K$. The energy hypothesis holds automatically for atoms and for local minima of the Born--Oppenheimer energy at which the electronic infimum is attained. The proof uses no symmetry of the density, restriction on the total nuclear charge, or minimum nuclear separation. We combine molecular Sommerfeld estimates with a convex nonlinear comparison in the variable $F(p)$. The failure of the latter comparison at very high density is represented by a nonnegative Newton potential. A quartic coercivity estimate, obtained from nuclear repulsion and a signed localized Hardy inequality, controls the total mass of this source. The chemical potential is retained throughout. Exact covariance yields the invariant parameter domain, and all finite numerical inequalities are reduced to rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition
papers.abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling of linear systems, such as Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity, is described by the bosonic Hopfield model, and gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition (SRPT). Modulating the magnetic field alone has been predicted to enhance the cycle-averaged coupling and induce a Floquet SRPT. We develop an exact theory of periodically driven Landau polaritons. Including the electric field induced by the modulated flux (Faraday's law), the problem reduces exactly, by Kohn's theorem, to the electronic center-of-mass mode coupled to the cavity, whose Hamiltonian is a sum of squares at every instant. A theorem of Krein then guarantees stability to all orders above a computable drive frequency, the Krein frequency, for which we give a self-contained proof. Below it, the system is stable except within resonance tongues where the drive creates pairs from the vacuum, the dynamical Casimir effect. At high drive frequency the electrons experience the mean field plus a ponderomotive trap (the Fock--Darwin problem), not an enhanced coupling. A gauge theorem excludes a Floquet photon condensate for any band structure, including Kane nonparabolicity, for which we derive a generalized Thomas--Reiche--Kuhn (TRK) sum rule. The predicted transition arises from averaging the coupling in a fixed Landau-level basis, which yields an effective model that violates the TRK sum rule; under driving, gauge invariance also requires the induced Faraday field. The rule to modulate and average the minimal-coupling Hamiltonian, not the parameters of its projection, applies to any linear, minimally coupled system. Instead of an SRPT, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission: Faraday-driven polariton--magnetoplasmon pairs at low threshold, and two-color photon pairs with up to 5--10~dB of two-mode squeezing.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论研究；基于精确哈密顿量与稳定性定理；研究对象：太赫兹腔内二维电子气形成的 Landau polaritons（朗道极化激元），受周期磁场调制

papers.title: Memory-gated transient anomalous transport of quasiparticles out of equilibrium
papers.abstract: Anomalous transport is ubiquitous across condensed matter, materials science, and biophysics. Yet, in far-from-equilibrium settings, what determines when, how much, and in which direction transport departs from diffusion remains a fundamental open question. By adopting the dispersive Holstein model of small polarons as representative of a wide class of dissipative systems, we show that a signed bath memory time governs the direction and the strength of the transient departure, and that when it vanishes, diffusion emerges without an asymptotic delay. Tuning the dissipative environment from resonant to off-resonant with the carrier density of states, transport turns from subdiffusion to superdiffusion as the memory time changes sign. Microscopically, we trace this memory effect to a competition between polaron formation and coherent polaron motion. These findings establish a unified memory-based description of transient anomalous transport, offering a path to control nonequilibrium quasiparticle flow through environmental tuning.

papers.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
papers.abstract: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently. Previous "post-mortem" studies have shown that fully trained Transformers indeed approximate canonical parsing algorithms such as inside-outside, but little is established theoretically about how this is actually learned. Here, we make a first step towards addressing this by studying the learning dynamics in synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. The stagewise learning curves are fully interpretable, in the sense that all of the loss stages a) can be computed analytically, and b) can be clearly associated to the representation of a hidden latent tree variable, which allows to lift ambiguity and utilize information from wider contexts. By probing representations, we visualize the emergence of inside-outside computation across depth and during training: while during early stages local (bigram/trigram) information is used and involves only a few initial layers, gradually the Transformer develops an encoder-decoder structure where the most abstract latent information is encoded in the middle, and the latter half of the network is used to progressively refine the final token prediction. This organization of computation is reminiscent of findings in real-world LLMs, and importantly applies here to a synthetic model which allows full analytical control of the data statistics, thus opening the door to theoretical progress.

papers.title: Geometric regulation of stress-limited growth on surfaces
papers.abstract: We analyze a model for microbial communities growing on surfaces in which individual growth is inhibited by collective growth-induced pressure. Asymptotic and numerical solutions on the sphere and homogenization of periodic surfaces show surface geometry can be tuned to either slow or accelerate growth. We use these insights to identify classes of surfaces for which the growth rate can be made arbitrarily small or arbitrarily close to the stress-free growth rate. These results show stress-sensing is coupled to surface curvature and topography at scales much larger than the individual, and provide design principles for controlling the growth of stress-sensitive microbial communities.

papers.title: Energetic costs of reaching the physical limits of sensing
papers.abstract: Cells sense chemical gradients by absorbing ligand molecules, a nonequilibrium process that necessarily produces entropy. But how many molecules must a cell absorb, and therefore energy dissipate, to approach the physical limits of sensing? We derive closed-form expressions relating gradient sensing uncertainty to the number of absorbed molecules, which we link to entropy production. Unlike concentration sensing, which depends only on the total count, gradient sensing must resolve the angular asymmetry of the absorbed flux, adding a bounded dipole-contrast factor set by how strongly the cell absorbs. In the strong-signal regime, cells approach peak chemotactic alignment while absorbing a small fraction of the diffusion-limited uptake, with the required number of uptake events set by the relative concentration change across the cell. Re-analysis of Dictyostelium chemotaxis places the cell at 0.25% of that limit with a minor metabolic load, suggesting that sensing is limited by counting noise rather than by energetic cost.
